words.gram: m. gen. sg., agreeing with indoḥ (stem yavāśir: yava + āśir "admixture")

hindi: सुन्दर जबड़ों वाले ने सोम-रस का पान किया, अत्यन्त कुशल, बह निकलने वाले (रस) का; इन्द्र (पान करता है) जौ से मिले हुए बूँद का।
english: The fair-jawed one has drunk of the Soma juice, of the very skilful, outpouring (juice); Indra (drinks) of the drop that is mixed with barley.
notes: Hard verse. śiprayandhasaḥ is read as śiprī andhasaḥ (the y is not regular sandhi; the Sāman text inserts it). The subject 'the fair-jawed one' is not named (Indra is the likely one but the text does not say so). Case and sense of yavāśiraḥ, indoḥ and the attachment of sudakṣasya prahoṣiṇaḥ to andhasaḥ are uncertain; the translation is tentative. yavāśiraḥ is the genitive singular of yavāśir (the nominative would be yavāśīḥ), so it agrees with indoḥ.

words.gram: f. nom. pl. (visarga lost before a vowel)

hindi: हे बहुत धन वाले, ये स्तुतियाँ तुम्हारी ओर गूँज उठी हैं, जैसे दुधारू गायें बछड़े की ओर।
english: These praises have sung out to you, O rich in wealth, as milch cows (low) to the calf.
notes: nonavuḥ is taken as the intensive perfect of √nu 'to roar, praise'. 'Low to' is supplied with 'like milch cows to the calf'.
lines_deva: इमा उ त्वा पुरुवसोऽभि प्र नोनवुर्गिरः
lines_iast: imā u tvā puruvaso'bhi pra nonavurgiraḥ

hindi: यहाँ ही उन्होंने गाय का, त्वष्टा के छिपे हुए नाम का ध्यान किया; इस प्रकार चन्द्रमा के घर में।
english: Here indeed they marked the hidden name of the cow, of Tvaṣṭṛ; thus in the house of the moon.
notes: The sentence is cryptic. 'goḥ' (of the cow) and 'tvaṣṭuḥ' (of Tvaṣṭṛ) are both genitives dependent on 'name'; whether they stand in apposition or separately is uncertain. Nothing is interpreted; who 'they' are is not stated. candramaso is candramasaḥ gen. sg. with the visarga (aḥ) becoming o before the voiced g.

hindi: जब सबसे अधिक उदार इन्द्र ने महान जलों को आगे बढ़ाया, तब वहाँ पूषन् साथी हुआ।
english: When Indra, the most bountiful, led the great waters, there Pūṣan was a companion.
notes: 'anayadrito' is kept as printed. The word 'rito' is uncertain: it may be ṛtaḥ (an adverbial 'rightly') or a participle of √rī 'flow/release'. Its construction is unclear; the translation leaves it out.

hindi: यश चाहने वाली गाय, उदार मरुतों की माता, दूध पिलाती है; रथों को ढोने वाली दोनों जुती हुई हैं।
english: The cow, desirous of fame, the mother of the bountiful Maruts, suckles (them); the two yoked bearers of the chariots (are ready).
notes: '~' in marutā~ is the candrabindu for anusvāra (marutām). 'them' (the Maruts) and 'are ready' are supplied. The second line is verbless; yuktā vahnī is read as dual nominatives ('the two yoked bearers'); the referent is not stated. dhayati 'suckles' (or 'drinks') is uncertain in its object.

hindi: हे उल्लासों के स्वामी, हरे घोड़ों के साथ हमारे निचोड़े हुए (सोम) के पास आओ; हमारे निचोड़े हुए (सोम) के पास हरे घोड़ों के साथ।
english: Come with your bay horses to our pressed (Soma), O lord of exhilarations; with your bay horses to our pressed (Soma).
notes: 'Soma' is supplied after 'pressed'. The addressee (Indra) is not named in the text. Line 2 repeats the first four words of line 1 (a refrain).
lines_deva: उप नो हरिभिः सुतं याहि मदानां पते
lines_iast: upa no haribhiḥ sutaṃ yāhi madānāṃ pate

hindi: इच्छित आहुतियाँ छोड़ी गईं, यज्ञ में इन्द्र को बढ़ाते हुए, बल के साथ अवभृथ की ओर।
english: The desired offerings were sent forth, strengthening Indra at the rite, towards the concluding bath (avabhṛtha) with might.
notes: iṣṭā hotrā may also be read 'the desired invocations'; vṛdhantaḥ (masculine) does not agree with hotrāḥ (feminine), so its subject may be the singers rather than the offerings; the translation keeps the grammatically loose literal order. The relation of 'with might' is uncertain. iṣṭā may also be the participle of √yaj ('offered').

words.gram: m. nom. sg. (visarga lost before i)

hindi: मैंने ही पिता से ऋत की मेधा को ग्रहण किया है; मैं सूर्य के समान उत्पन्न हुआ।
english: I indeed have seized, from the father, the wisdom of truth (ṛta); I was born like the sun.
notes: jagraha is the Sāman form for jagrabha. 'aham ... ajani': ajani is the passive aorist, normally 3 sg., with 'I' as the subject of the clause ('I was born' is the literal sense). pituḥ may be 'of the father' or 'from the father'; 'from' is taken with pari.

words.gram: m. loc. sg. (e becomes a before i)

words.gloss: rich in food, rich in cattle

hindi: हमारे लिए धनवती, प्रचुर बल वाली (वे) इन्द्र के साथ सहभोज में हों, जिनसे हम अन्न से समृद्ध होकर आनन्द मनाएँ।
english: May the wealthy ones, abounding in strength, be ours at the common feast with Indra, by which, being rich in food, we may rejoice.
notes: The feminine revatīḥ has no noun; 'ones' (probably cows or riches) is not supplied further. sadhamāda is sadhamāde before indre (Vedic e to a). kṣumantaḥ is read with 'we'.

hindi: सोम और पूषन् दोनों सब सुव्यवस्थित बस्तियों (जनों) के विषय में जानते हैं; देवों के बीच रथ खींचने वाली दोनों (जोड़ी) के रूप में स्थित।
english: Soma and Pūṣan both are aware of all the well-settled (peoples); placed among the gods, of the two chariot-drawers.
notes: rathyoḥ hitā is very uncertain (rathyā is also 'chariot-driver'); the translation keeps the literal words. 'peoples' for kṣiti is supplied as the usual sense of the word.

hindi: तुम्हारे सोम-रस के पान करने वाले इन्द्र की ओर गान करो, सबको जीतने वाले, सौ शक्तियों वाले, मनुष्यों में सबसे उदार का।
english: Sing forth to Indra, the drinker of your juice, the all-conquering, the one of a hundred powers, the most bountiful of the peoples.
notes: '~' in viśvāsāha~ and ma~hiṣṭhaṃ is the candrabindu for anusvāra. The particle ā after pāntam is taken as 'towards'; it may also be a mere expletive. śatakratu 'of a hundred powers/rites' is used as an epithet; both senses are possible.
lines_deva: पान्तमा वो अन्धस इन्द्रमभि प्र गायत
lines_iast: pāntamā vo andhasa indramabhi pra gāyata

hindi: हे मित्रो, तुम सब इन्द्र के लिए, हरे घोड़ों वाले, सोम पीने वाले के लिए, उल्लास देने वाला (गीत) गाओ।
english: O friends, sing forth to Indra, the bay-horsed Soma-drinker, the exhilarating (song).
notes: 'song' is supplied for mādanam (exhilarating, neuter). va is vaḥ, an enclitic 'for you / on your part'.
lines_deva: प्र व इन्द्राय मादनँ हर्यश्वाय गायत
lines_iast: pra va indrāya mādana~ haryaśvāya gāyata

words.gram: m. nom. pl. pres. part. denom.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, हम तुम्हें चाहने वाले, उसी प्रयोजन वाले मित्र हैं; कण्व स्तोत्रों से तुम्हारी स्तुति करते हैं।
english: We indeed, O Indra, your friends desiring you with that very aim; the Kaṇvas praise (you) with hymns.
notes: 'you' is supplied as object of jarante. kaṇvāḥ is a plural name; the text says nothing more about them.
lines_deva: वयमु त्वा तदिदर्था इन्द्र त्वायन्तः सखायः
lines_iast: vayamu tvā tadidarthā indra tvāyantaḥ sakhāyaḥ

words.gloss: let them resound, let them praise
words.gram: 3 pl. impv. √stubh (s becomes ṣ after pari)

hindi: इन्द्र के लिए, उल्लास देने वाले के लिए, निचोड़े हुए (सोम) के चारों ओर हमारी स्तुतियाँ गूँजें; गायक अर्क (स्तुति-गान) का गान करें।
english: For Indra, the gladdening one, around the pressed (Soma), let our praises resound; let the singers chant the hymn.
notes: The grouping 'indrāya madvane sutam' is read as 'for Indra the gladdening, (around) the pressed (Soma)'; sutam may be attached differently. arka is taken as 'hymn' (it can also be 'ray').
lines_deva: इन्द्राय मद्वने सुतं परि ष्टोभन्तु नो गिरः
lines_iast: indrāya madvane sutaṃ pari ṣṭobhantu no giraḥ

hindi: हे इन्द्र, यह तुम्हारा सोम कुश के आसन पर शुद्ध किया हुआ है; आओ, दौड़कर इसमें से पियो।
english: This Soma of yours, O Indra, is purified upon the sacred grass; come, hasten, drink of it.
notes: īm is an emphatic particle and is not translated separately. dravā may be an adverb 'quickly'.
lines_deva: अयं त इन्द्र सोमो निपूतो अधि बर्हिषि
lines_iast: ayaṃ ta indra somo nipūto adhi barhiṣi

words.gloss: maker of good forms, skilful worker

hindi: सुन्दर रूप बनाने वाले (कुशल) को हम सहायता के लिए प्रतिदिन बुलाते हैं, जैसे दूध दुहने वाले के लिए अच्छी दुधारू गाय को।
english: We call day after day, for help, the skilful maker of fair forms, as one calls a good milch cow for the milker.
notes: The one called is not named in the text. 'surūpakṛtnum' is taken as 'maker of good forms / fair worker'; the exact sense of rūpa here (forms or beauty) is open. 'One calls' is supplied in the comparison.

hindi: हे बैल, सोम निचोड़ने पर मैं निचोड़ा हुआ (सोम) तुम्हारी ओर पीने के लिए प्रवाहित करता हूँ; तृप्त हो, उल्लास को पूरी तरह पाओ।
english: To you, O bull, at the pressing I pour out the pressed (Soma) for drinking; be satisfied, enjoy the exhilaration fully.
notes: vṛṣabhā is read as a vocative with Vedic lengthening; as an instrumental ('with the bull') it would not suit. The addressee (Indra) is not named. sute may be 'at the pressing' or an adjective 'pressed'.
lines_deva: अभि त्वा वृषभा सुते सुतँ सृजामि पीतये
lines_iast: abhi tvā vṛṣabhā sute suta~ sṛjāmi pītaye

hindi: हे इन्द्र, जो सोम चमसों में और पात्रों में तुम्हारे लिए निचोड़ा गया है, उसी में से पियो; तुम (उस पर) अधिकार रखते हो।
english: O Indra, the Soma that is pressed for you in the cups and in the vessels, drink of it; you have power (over it).
notes: 'over it' is supplied after īśiṣe. 'ā' after camaseṣu is taken as a postposition 'in'. 'pibed' is piba + id.
lines_deva: य इन्द्र चमसेष्वा सोमश्चमूषु ते सुतः
lines_iast: ya indra camaseṣvā somaścamūṣu te sutaḥ

hindi: हर उद्यम में, हर संघर्ष में, हम मित्र अधिक बलवान इन्द्र को सहायता के लिए बुलाते हैं।
english: In every undertaking, in every contest, we friends call the mightier Indra for help.
notes: tavastara is a comparative ('mightier'); 'very mighty' is also possible. yoga here is 'undertaking/enterprise' (literally yoking).

words.gram: 2 pl. impv. √sad (s becomes ṣ after ni)

hindi: आओ, अब बैठ जाओ और इन्द्र की ओर गान करो, हे मित्रो, स्तोम (स्तुति) को वहन करने वालो।
english: Come now, sit down and sing forth to Indra, O friends, bearers of praise-songs.
notes: 'ā ... eta' is split by tu: 'ā tu eta'. sakhāyaḥ stomavāhasaḥ are vocatives.
lines_deva: आ त्वेता नि षीदतेन्द्रमभि प्र गायत
lines_iast: ā tvetā ni ṣīdatendramabhi pra gāyata

hindi: हे दानों के स्वामी, यह तुम्हारे बल से निचोड़ा हुआ है; हे स्तुति-प्रिय, अब इसमें से पियो।
english: For this is pressed by your might, O lord of bounties; drink of it, O lover of praise.
notes: 'hyanvojasā' is hi anu ojasā; 'anu ojasā' is read as 'according to / by your might'. The pluta '3' in tvā3sya is a chant mark and is not translated. rādhas may mean 'bounty' or 'success'. Tentative: 'idaṃ ... sutam' is 'this pressed (Soma)'.

words.gloss: for the wielder of the thunderbolt

hindi: महान इन्द्र है, और आगे भी; वज्रधारी के लिए महिमा हो; आकाश के समान विस्तार से (उसका) बल है।
english: Great is Indra, and before (us) too; let greatness be for the wielder of the thunderbolt; his might (is) like heaven in breadth.

text_flags.why: possible: a remembered parallel reads 'paraś ca nu' (and beyond); the printed puraś ca no is kept and read as 'puraḥ ca naḥ'. Unverified.

notes: Uncertain. puraś ca no is read as puraḥ ca naḥ with 'naḥ' left over; the sentence division is tentative. 'his' is supplied before 'might'.
lines_deva: महाँ इन्द्रः पुरश्च नो महित्वमस्तु वज्रिणे
lines_iast: mahā~ indraḥ puraśca no mahitvamastu vajriṇe

words.gloss: rich in food, rich in cattle

hindi: हे इन्द्र, अब हमारे लिए अन्न से भरपूर, अद्भुत मुट्ठीभर एकत्र कर लो, तुम बड़े हाथ वाले, दाहिने (हाथ) से।
english: Now, O Indra, gather for us with your right hand a wonderful handful, rich in food, you of the great hand.
notes: 'grābham' is the grasp or handful; 'of wealth' is not in the text. 'hand' is supplied after dakṣiṇena. mahāhastī is read as nominative qualifying the addressee.
lines_deva: आ तू न इन्द्र क्षुमन्तं चित्रं ग्राभँ सं गृभाय
lines_iast: ā tū na indra kṣumantaṃ citraṃ grābha~ saṃ gṛbhāya

hindi: गायों के स्वामी इन्द्र की ओर गान के साथ स्तुति करो, जैसे वह जाना जाता है; सत्य के पुत्र, सज्जनों के स्वामी की।
english: Praise with song Indra, the lord of cattle, as he is known, the son of truth, the lord of the good.
notes: 'yathā vide' could be 'as I know / as he is known'. The compounds are kept literal: gopati 'lord of cattle', satpati 'lord of the good'.
lines_deva: अभि प्र गोपतिं गिरेन्द्रमर्च यथा विदे
lines_iast: abhi pra gopatiṃ girendramarca yathā vide

hindi: किस सहायता से वह अद्भुत, सदा बढ़ने वाला मित्र हमारे पास आए? किस सबसे शक्तिशाली क्रम से?
english: By what help may the wonderful, ever-growing friend come to us? By what most powerful course?
notes: The friend is not named. vṛtā is uncertain (instrumental of vṛt 'course/turning', or a participle 'chosen'); the translation takes 'course'. naś citra is naḥ citraḥ; naḥ is read with 'ā bhuvat' as 'to us'.
lines_deva: कया नश्चित्र आ भुवदूती सदावृधः सखा
lines_iast: kayā naścitra ā bhuvadūtī sadāvṛdhaḥ sakhā

words.gloss: you bring, you set in motion

hindi: तुम्हारे उस सब को जीतने वाले को, जो सब स्तुतियों में फैला हुआ है, तुम सहायता के लिए यहाँ ले आते हो।
english: That all-conquering one of yours, present in all songs, you bring here for help.
notes: The addressee and the referent are not stated. vaḥ is 'of you (plural)', yet cyāvayasi is 2 sg.; the number mismatch may point to a different original reading (for example cyāvayāmasi, 'we bring'), unverified. gīrṣu āyatam: 'extended/present in the songs' is tentative.

words.gloss: I have approached, I have obtained

hindi: मैंने सभा-पति को प्राप्त किया है, जो अद्भुत है, इन्द्र का प्रिय और कामना के योग्य है; (मैंने) दान-रूप मेधा पाई है।
english: I have obtained the lord of the assembly, wonderful, dear to Indra, desirable; I have obtained the gift, wisdom.
notes: ayāsiṣam: 1 sg. aorist of √yā 'go'; 'obtained' is a looser rendering (some take it from √yāc, 'I have begged'). saniṃ medhām is read as 'the gift, wisdom'; saniṃ may instead qualify medhām ('winning wisdom'). 'priyam indrasya' may be 'dear, belonging to Indra'.

hindi: तुम्हारे जो मार्ग आकाश के नीचे हैं, जिनसे तुमने व्यश्व को चलाया, और (वे) प्राणी हमें सुनें।
english: Those paths of yours below heaven, by which you drove Vyaśva; and let the beings hear us.
notes: Uncertain. vyaśvam is read as a name (Vyaśva) but may be an adjective 'horseless'. bhuvaḥ as 'beings/worlds' is a guess; the second line may be a separate wish. 'adho divaḥ' is taken as 'below heaven' (the text may also mean 'down from heaven').
lines_deva: ये ते पन्था अधो दिवो येभिर्व्यश्वमैरयः
lines_iast: ye te panthā adho divo yebhirvyaśvamairayaḥ

hindi: हे सौ शक्तियों वाले, हमारे लिए हर भली वस्तु लाओ, अन्न और बल; हे इन्द्र, ताकि तुम हम पर कृपालु हो।
english: Bring us every good thing, food and vigour, O hundred-powered; so that you, O Indra, may be gracious to us.
notes: 'yat' is taken as 'so that'; it could also be 'because' or 'whereby'. mṛḍayāsi is taken as a causative subjunctive ('may you show mercy').

hindi: यह निचोड़ा हुआ सोम यहाँ है; मरुत् इसमें से पीते हैं, और स्वयं शासन करने वाले दोनों अश्विन् भी।
english: Here is this pressed Soma; the Maruts drink of it, and the self-ruling ones, the two Aśvins.
notes: svarājaḥ (plural) next to aśvinā (dual) is read as 'the self-ruling ones, the two Aśvins'; it could instead name other gods. 'Here' is supplied with asti.
lines_deva: अस्ति सोमो अयँ सुतः पिबन्त्यस्य मरुतः
lines_iast: asti somo aya~ sutaḥ pibantyasya marutaḥ

words.gram: f. nom./acc. pl. pres. part. caus.
m. nom. pl. pres. part. mid. √van

hindi: हिलाती हुई, कर्म की इच्छुक (वे) उत्पन्न इन्द्र की उपासना करती हैं, श्रेष्ठ वीरता को प्राप्त करते हुए।
english: Stirring, eager for work, they attend upon the born Indra, winning heroic strength.
notes: Obscure. The feminine īṅkhayantīḥ and apasyuvaḥ do not agree with the masculine vanvānāsaḥ; the subject of upāsate is not stated, and who is 'stirred' is unclear. The translation is tentative. jātam is 'born'; no 'new' is in the text.

words.gloss: in accordance with what the mantra says

hindi: हे देवो, हम कभी भंग नहीं करते और न कुछ बिगाड़ते हैं; हम मन्त्र में सुने गए के अनुसार आचरण करते हैं।
english: O gods, we do not at all violate (anything), nor do we disturb (anything); we act in accordance with what is heard in the mantra.

text_flags.why: possible: the verb 'we violate' is normally minīmasi (√mī); the printed word lacks the initial m. A remembered Rigvedic parallel is not verified.

notes: 'inīmasi' may be the printed form of minīmasi (see text_flags). No object is stated for the two verbs; none is supplied. kyā is ki + ā by sandhi. mantraśrutyam is uncertain; 'in accordance with what the mantra declares' is the literal sense.
lines_deva: न कि देवा इनीमसि न क्या योपयामसि
lines_iast: na ki devā inīmasi na kyā yopayāmasi

words.gram: f. nom. sg. (or inst. 'in the evening')

hindi: संध्या आ गई है; महान (सामगान) गाओ, हे आथर्वण, उज्ज्वल गान में; देव सविता की स्तुति करो।
english: Evening has come; sing the great (chant), bright in song, O descendant of Atharvan; praise the god Savitṛ.
notes: Uncertain. doṣo is read as doṣā + u. gāman is taken as locative 'in the song' (it could be otherwise); 'chant' is supplied after bṛhat. Ātharvaṇa is a patronymic address, not a name for a specific person.

words.gram: n. acc. sg. used as adverb

hindi: यह अनुपम उषा प्रकट होकर चमकती है, आकाश की प्रिय; हे अश्विनो, मैं तुम दोनों की बड़ी स्तुति करता हूँ।
english: This matchless Dawn shines forth, dear one of heaven; I praise you two, O Aśvins, greatly.
notes: eṣo uṣā: eṣaḥ is masculine though Dawn is feminine (Vedic usage). apūrvyā may also be 'not earlier than' / 'unprecedented'. 'divaḥ' may be 'of the sky' or 'daughter of heaven' (the second not stated).
lines_deva: एषो उषा अपूर्व्या व्युच्छति प्रिया दिवः
lines_iast: eṣo uṣā apūrvyā vyucchati priyā divaḥ

hindi: अप्रतिरोध्य इन्द्र ने दधीचि की हड्डियों से वृत्रों को मारा, नौ और नब्बे को।
english: Indra, irresistible, slew the Vṛtras with the bones of Dadhīci, nine and ninety.
notes: navatīr nava is traditionally read as ninety-nine; the literal words are 'nineties, nine'. 'vṛtra' is taken as a common noun 'obstacle, foe' in the plural.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, आओ, सोम-रस से तृप्त होओ, सोम के सब पर्वों (गाँठों) के साथ; तुम महान और बल से विजयी हो।
english: Come, O Indra, delight in the juice with all the joints of Soma; you are great, prevailing by might.
notes: 'andhasaḥ' is a genitive, 'delight in / of the juice'. 'soma-parvan' is the literal 'joints of Soma' (the plant's knots); not interpreted. 'you are' is supplied; abhiṣṭi is read as 'prevailing'. mahā~ is mahān.

hindi: हे वृत्रहन् इन्द्र, अब हमारे पास हमारे पक्ष में आओ, तुम महान, महान सहायताओं के साथ।
english: Come now to us, O Indra, O slayer of Vṛtra, to our side; come, great, with great helps.
notes: ardham 'side / share / half' is uncertain; 'to our side' is the reading taken.
lines_deva: आ तू न इन्द्र वृत्रहन्नस्माकमर्धमा गहि
lines_iast: ā tū na indra vṛtrahannasmākamardhamā gahi

hindi: उसका वह बल चमका, जब इन्द्र ने दोनों लोकों को चमड़े की तरह लपेट लिया।
english: That might of his shone when Indra rolled both worlds together like a hide.
notes: titviṣa is titviṣe before u. 'Rolled together like a hide' is the literal sense (as one rolls up a skin). The verb titviṣe may also be 'was strong / wondrous'.

hindi: यह निश्चय ही तुम्हारे लिए है; तुम कबूतर की तरह घोंसले की ओर एक साथ आते हो; हमारे उस वचन को भी तुम वहन करते हो।
english: This indeed is for you; you come together like a dove to its nest; that speech of ours too you carry.
notes: Very uncertain; the verse is obscure. 'ayam' has no noun (what 'this' is, is not stated); samatasi and garbhadhim are tentative; 'to its' is supplied in the simile. vacas tac cin na ohase is read 'that speech of ours indeed you carry'.
lines_deva: अयमु ते समतसि कपोत इव गर्भधिम्
lines_iast: ayamu te samatasi kapota iva garbhadhim

words.gram: m. nom. sg. (visarga lost before ā)

hindi: वायु हमारे हृदय के लिए कल्याणकारी, सुखदायक औषध बहाकर लाए; वह हमारी आयु को बढ़ाए।
english: May the wind blow here a remedy, beneficial and bringing happiness, for our heart; may he prolong our lives.

text_flags.why: possible: b for bh (bheṣaja, 'remedy'); the printed initial is b.
possible: the word is normally āyus 'life' (āyūṃṣi); the printed initial a is short (after na, āyū~ṣi would print as na āyū~ṣi). Unverified.

notes: vāta is the wind (the natural wind), not the vāta humour; this is a non-medical Vedic prayer. The remedy is not named or described further. 'He' (the wind) is the subject of tāriṣat.
lines_deva: वात आ वातु बेषजँ शम्भु मयोभु नो हृदे
lines_iast: vāta ā vātu beṣaja~ śambhu mayobhu no hṛde

words.gram: m. nom. sg. (name of a god)

hindi: जिसकी बुद्धिमान वरुण, मित्र और अर्यमा रक्षा करते हैं, वह मनुष्य कभी हिंसित नहीं होता।
english: The man whom the wise ones, Varuṇa, Mitra and Aryaman, protect is never harmed.
notes: 'na kiḥ' is nakiḥ 'never / by no one'. The relative clause is rendered as a subject phrase.
lines_deva: यँ रक्षन्ति प्रचेतसो वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा
lines_iast: ya~ rakṣanti pracetaso varuṇo mitro aryamā

words.gram: 2 sg. impv. denom. √gavya (lengthened), parallel to aśvayā, rathayā

hindi: हमारे लिए अच्छी तरह गौओं की खोज करो, जैसे पहले; और घोड़ों तथा रथों की खोज करो; उदार (जनों) के लिए धन प्रदान करो।
english: Seek cattle well for us, as of old; and seek horses and chariots; bestow wealth on the bountiful.

text_flags.why: possible: the word recurs as maghonām (bountiful ones) in the same chunk; the printed mahonām may be a variant or a typo.

notes: Very uncertain. gavyo ṣu ṇo is read gavyā u su naḥ (gavyā, aśvayā, rathayā and varivasyā are parallel lengthened 2 sg. imperatives of denominatives); ṇo is naḥ after ṣu. mahonām is kept as printed (possibly maghonām, see text_flags); its relation to varivasyā is tentative. The addressee is not named. The token purāśvayota is purā + aśvayā + uta.
lines_deva: गव्यो षु णो यथा पुराश्वयोत रथया
lines_iast: gavyo ṣu ṇo yathā purāśvayota rathayā

hindi: हे इन्द्र, ये तुम्हारी चितकबरी (वे) घी और मिश्रण दुहती हैं, इस ऋत की (धारा से) भरी हुई।
english: These dappled ones of yours, O Indra, milk out ghee, the mixture, swelling with this (flow) of the order.
notes: pṛśnayaḥ 'dappled ones' is kept literal (cows; later tradition links them to the Maruts, not imported). 'flow' is supplied; enām is taken as 'this' agreeing with an unstated noun. Tentative.
lines_deva: इमास्त इन्द्र पृश्नयो घृतं दुहत आशिरम्
lines_iast: imāsta indra pṛśnayo ghṛtaṃ duhata āśiram

hindi: हे बहुत नामों वाले, हे बहुत स्तुत, और इस गौओं की कामना वाली बुद्धि (स्तुति) से, जब तुम हर सोम पर आते हो।
english: And with this thought (praise) that seeks cattle, O many-named, much-praised one, when you come to every Soma.
notes: dhiyā is 'thought' or 'prayer'; the main verb is not given ('we call you' or similar is not supplied). 'ā bhuvaḥ' is 'you come to be present'.

words.gloss: let her accept, let her desire

hindi: शुद्ध करने वाली सरस्वती, जो बलों से युक्त और पोषक अन्न वाली है, बुद्धि से धन देने वाली, हमारे यज्ञ को चाहे।
english: May the purifying Sarasvatī, rich in strengths and vigour, who gives wealth through thought, desire our sacrifice.
notes: dhiyāvasuḥ is read 'wealth through thought/prayer' (i.e. gives wealth for prayer). vājinīvatī: 'possessing vigorous (nourishing) ...'. Sarasvatī is kept as a name; the text says nothing more.

hindi: नहुष के जनों में कौन इस इन्द्र को सोम से तृप्त करेगा? वह हमारे लिए धन ले आए।
english: Who among the Nahuṣa peoples will satisfy this Indra with Soma? May he bring us riches.
notes: nāhuṣīṣu is the feminine plural locative of nāhuṣa ('of Nahuṣa'); 'peoples' is supplied. tarpayāt is read as a 3 sg. subjunctive/aorist; 'with Soma' is the genitive of the substance.
lines_deva: क इमं नाहुषीष्वा इन्द्रँ सोमस्य तर्पयात्
lines_iast: ka imaṃ nāhuṣīṣvā indra~ somasya tarpayāt

hindi: आओ, क्योंकि हमने तुम्हारे लिए सोम निचोड़ा है, हे इन्द्र; इस सोम को पियो। इस कुश तक आओ, मेरे आसन तक।
english: Come, O Indra, for we have pressed Soma for you; drink this Soma. Come to this sacred grass, to my seat.
notes: edam is ā + idam; 'come' is repeated from the first line. sadaḥ may also be an imperative 'sit'.
lines_deva: आ याहि सुषुमा हि त इन्द्र सोमं पिबा इमम्
lines_iast: ā yāhi suṣumā hi ta indra somaṃ pibā imam

hindi: तीनों की — मित्र, अर्यमा और वरुण की — महान, आकाशवासी, दुर्धर्ष रक्षा (हमारे लिए) हो।
english: May the great, heavenly protection of the three, of Mitra, Aryaman and Varuṇa, hard to assail, be (ours).

text_flags.why: possible: the form avar before astu is unusual; avaḥ (protection) is expected, written avo 'stu.

notes: avar (for avaḥ) before astu is read as avaḥ; 'ours' is supplied. dyukṣam may be 'dwelling in heaven' or 'shining'.

hindi: हे बहुत धन वाले इन्द्र, हे नेता, हम तुम जैसे के (जन) हैं; हे हरे घोड़ों के स्थाता।
english: We are those of one like you, O Indra, rich in wealth, O leader; O stander of the bay horses.
notes: 'those' (people) is supplied with tvāvataḥ. sthātar harīṇām is read as 'stander of the bay horses'.
